question: Does using task-class-balanced weights for public cross-encoder correspondence explain part of the HR versus strengthened-KD gap?
primary_hypothesis: In the current sparse-positive public cohort, separating patient-equal correspondence calibration from class-balanced task readouts improves downstream transfer. This predicts positive U-minus-B effects within BOTH HR and ACKD, not merely superiority of the existing HR package.
selection_basis: Selected from2-1R2 public-only operation diagnostics before any new labels or V efficacy. This remains adaptive development.
carrier: Frozen first public128 from contribution_public128_control_20260928_v1/public128_selection.npz; no reselection.

fixed.task_weights: Existing image weights Omega: 0.5 per class, equal patients within class and visits within patient/class.
fixed.solver: Same public128 RN-only zero-anchor BVLS, bounds[-1,1], eta=.001*||A||F^2/128, RMS normalization, tol1e-12,maxiter500,KKT<=1e-7
fixed.metric: Image AUROC primary, AP secondary, paired patient-cluster bootstrap

treatment_detail: U vs B changes ONLY correspondence fitting weights. HR fitted centering/intercepts and implied mapped public anchor are re-estimated as consequences of that weight change. Do not claim slope-only or pure class-imbalance information removal. ACKD geometry uses U or B while its task Hessians and actual public anchor remain fixed.
contrasts: REFERENCE: each new variant minus fixed DINO-only
analysis: Within every bootstrap replicate, calculate each release metric difference, then average the two differences. Do not average predictions, pool releases as independent patients, or pair independent noise draws across mechanisms.

strong_support_gate.interpretation: Existing engineering hurdle, not a clinical threshold. Failure is insufficient evidence, not equality/disproof of every weighting effect.

decision_rules: Both primary contrasts pass: support the scoped calibration-weight mechanism; this does not establish new general weighting theory or a CVPR contribution.
ACKD_U closes the statistically supported HR advantage: accept the stronger standard baseline; do not call an overlapping interval equivalence.
Only one primary contrast passes or signs conflict: no shared calibration-weight mechanism claim; report the recipe-specific result without selecting a new headline.
HR remains better at matched U weights: residual package difference remains, but this result alone does not identify clipping/centering as its cause.
No result triggers a new DP draw, new receiver, weight grid, or Expert/Reserved. Original2-3 gate and2-3R1 mixed result remain.
freeze_sequence: Validate target schema/hashes and exact reproduction of existing HR_U and ACKD_B.
Construct all four labels; seal targets, labels, solver settings and hashes before any V evaluation.
Evaluate all new labels under the frozen two receivers, reuse the12 existing comparisons, and report all predeclared contrasts.
